{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRkquM8AAAABZlwAsg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5zhDMTeg", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5", "number": 103, "title": "Delay preconfigured NTSC H-only HTIME=0 IRQ assertion to master clock 14", "body": "## Problem

Preconfigured H-only timer IRQs with HTIME=0 still assert at scanline rollover instead of the documented delayed horizontal event. This is the next incomplete behavior identified by `latest_assessment`; the supplied context lists no open Issue duplicating it.

At baseline `7f2e79aa55fbcaa5393bc81bb9deaff00252864f`, [`SystemBus::tick`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/7f2e79aa55fbcaa5393bc81bb9deaff00252864f/crates/snes-core/src/machine.rs#L195) excludes zero from horizontal delay calculation and explicitly asserts H-only zero at rollover. `horizontal_zero_timer_fires_once_per_scanline_across_frames` and [`horizontal_irq_zero_and_late_controls_retain_only_approximate_scheduling`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/7f2e79aa55fbcaa5393bc81bb9deaff00252864f/crates/snes-core/src/machine/horizontal_irq_tests.rs#L161) preserve this behavior as an approximation. Their passing results do not establish its correctness.

Correcting this event makes CPU waits and IRQ-dependent device accesses observe the supported timer delay, while preserving the separate combined-zero correction from #101.

## Expected outcome

For NTSC non-interlaced operation, with `NMITIMEN & $30 == $10` and both HTIME bytes zero before naturally entering a scanline:

- With no earlier IRQ pending, TIMEUP bit 7 stays clear through elapsed master H=13 and asserts when advancement crosses H=14.
- This occurs once on every naturally entered scanline, independently of VTIME, including ordinary lines, the 1360-clock short line and natural field rollover into V=0.
- Remove the H=0 rollover assertion for this case. Early reads must not consume the future event. Preserve pending retention and existing acknowledgement semantics.
- Preserve the initial reset-created V=0 no-event convention explicitly as unverified reset policy.
- V-only and combined HTIME=0 remain at H=10; eligible nonzero horizontal comparisons retain `4*HTIME+14`.

Hardware basis: [Fullsnes, SNES Timing H/V Events and SNES PPU Interrupts](https://problemkaputt.de/fullsnes.htm) supplies the H-only `HTIME+3.5` timer-unit expression recorded in the repository's [#99 reconciliation](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/7f2e79aa55fbcaa5393bc81bb9deaff00252864f/docs/issue-99-validation.md#source-reconciliation-recorded-before-implementation). Four master clocks per timer unit yield `4*(0+3.5)=14`. The recorded 2.5-unit exception applies to V-only and combined HTIME=0; [#101 reconciliation](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/7f2e79aa55fbcaa5393bc81bb9deaff00252864f/docs/issue-101-validation.md#source-reconciliation-before-implementation-2026-10-24) does not extend it to H-only. [Anomie's Register Doc, revision 1157](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gilligan/snesdev/master/docs/snes_registers.txt), NMITIMEN/HTIME/VTIME/TIMEUP, supports comparison-following assertion and mode gating; it is not an independent numerical measurement of the 14-clock delay.

These source distinctions supersede the old H-only-zero test approximation. Document the derivation and any contradictory evidence rather than preserving an unsupported earlier contract.

Scope is this assertion correction and its integration tests. Physical coincident TIMEUP reads, write-clear disagreement, CPU recognition phases, DMA alignment, live configuration and physical reset alignment remain unresolved. Access-end sampling, immediate read acknowledgement and instruction-boundary service remain emulator conventions.

## Context and reproduction

Planning inspected repository source, tests and recorded specification reconciliations only. HEAD matches the baseline above. External specifications were not re-fetched, no tests were rerun and no files were changed.

A minimal original unit reproduction can use the existing `timer_bus` helper:

1. Configure H-only mode, HTIME=0 and VTIME=511 before naturally entering V=1.
2. Advance to absolute clock 1363 and acknowledge earlier pending state.
3. Advance one clock to V=1/H=0. Current code sets TIMEUP; expected bit 7 is clear.
4. In fresh observations, advance to H=13/14/15. Expected bit 7 is respectively clear/set/set before acknowledgement.

The existing [`combined_zero_irq_tests.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/7f2e79aa55fbcaa5393bc81bb9deaff00252864f/crates/snes-core/src/machine/combined_zero_irq_tests.rs) provides useful boundary, CPU-read, real DMA and deferred-service patterns. Its [`combined_zero_irq.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/7f2e79aa55fbcaa5393bc81bb9deaff00252864f/crates/snes-core/tests/combined_zero_irq.rs) guest and [provenance record](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/7f2e79aa55fbcaa5393bc81bb9deaff00252864f/tests/roms/PROVENANCE.md#original-combined-zero-irq-diagnostic-issue-101) demonstrate original source-built construction without firmware.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Implement the bounded H-only-zero crossing at H=14 and remove its rollover assertion. Document source sections, timer-unit arithmetic, the H-only/combined-zero distinction and unresolved physical behavior. Update README limits and supersede only obsolete H-only-zero approximation statements. Correct the two existing zero controls while retaining their coverage and all late-comparison controls.
- [ ] Add original tests under a consistent `horizontal_zero_irq` name. Use fresh buses at H=0/9/10/13/14/15 on naturally reached V=0/1/224/225/239/240/241/261 in both field parities. Clear earlier pending state before target-line entry, never at H=0 where acknowledgement could hide the defect. Exercise VTIME=0/240/262/511 to prove H-only independence. Verify early reads preserve delivery, acknowledgement occurs once, no later same-line or next-H=0 duplicate occurs, and the next line asserts again at H=14. Retain explicit initial-V=0 policy coverage and pending retention across lines, fields and later assertions.
- [ ] Preserve once-per-line coverage across at least three complete natural fields. Expected line lengths and event positions must use independent arithmetic, not production scheduling or PPU conversion helpers.
- [ ] Compare one-clock, irregular `1/7/1361/2/43/8193/5` and whole-interval advancement across ordinary, short-line and field boundaries. Include literal events 1378 (initial V=1), 357382/714746 (natural V=0), 327374/684742 (V=240) and 328738/686102 (V=241), with earlier pending flags cleared before each target. Check final raster geometry and independently calculated audio sample counts; compare PCM across partitions as determinism evidence only.
- [ ] Test six-clock CPU TIMEUP reads ending before, at and after H=14, including a read ending at H=0. Test real fixed-A `$004211`→WMDATA general DMA around ordinary, short-line and field-boundary events. Under existing DMA phases, starts at event−21/−20/−19 must produce destination bit-7 sequences `[0,$80,0]`, `[$80,0,0]`, `[$80,0,0]`. Check destination bytes, pointers, channel completion, clocks and acknowledgement. Label coincident access results as existing model conventions.
- [ ] Add a real DMA crossing the corrected event while an unmasked CPU waits. Verify payload, clocks, PPU/APU advancement and retained IRQ; CPU PC, instruction count and stack must remain unchanged during DMA. Resumption must perform one IRQ entry under existing CPU conventions. Do not claim this validates physical DMA alignment or recognition timing.
- [ ] Add an original MIT source-built 65C816 guest, for example `tests/horizontal_zero_irq.rs`, observing V=240 across four natural fields, including both short-line parities. Establish H-only zero before each target line, record counters/parity/TIMEUP acknowledgement and compare every literal record in executed guest code. Include explicit success/failure markers and bounded step/clock deadlines. Host code must only load, step and observe; no beam, IRQ, CPU-state or result injection. Record authorship, construction and independent expected-clock derivations in `tests/roms/PROVENANCE.md`.
- [ ] Demonstrate that the new fresh-boundary regression and guest compile and fail behaviorally on exact baseline `7f2e79aa55fbcaa5393bc81bb9deaff00252864f`, transferring only test sources and necessary test registration. Record actual failures and corrected passes. A compile failure is not a behavioral counterexample.
- [ ] Run the following focused and workspace gates, recording actual results and any failures:

```sh
cargo test --locked -p snes-core horizontal_zero_irq
cargo test --locked -p snes-core v_only_irq
cargo test --locked -p snes-core horizontal_irq
cargo test --locked -p snes-core combined_zero_irq
cargo test --locked -p snes-core --test ntsc_timing
cargo test --locked -p snes-core --lib machine::ntsc_timing_tests
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace --locked
```

- [ ] Run the existing source-built hardware and browser gates from [README validation](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/README.md#validate), using its documented compiler/port adjustments when needed:

```sh
python3 tools/make-fixture.py .cache/smoke.bin
cmp tests/roms/smoke.bin .cache/smoke.bin
python3 tools/build-test-tools.py --spc
python3 tools/hardware-tests.py \
  --ca65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ca65" \
  --ld65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ld65" \
  --spcasm "$PWD/.cache/tools/spcasm/target/release/spcasm"
python3 tools/ppu-test.py --bass "$PWD/.cache/tools/bass-untech/bass/out/bass-untech"
python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
npm --prefix web ci
npm --prefix web run build
npm --prefix web exec playwright install chromium
npm --prefix web test -- --grep-invert '301 seconds'
```

Preserve existing CPU/WAI, V-only, combined-zero, nonzero/late IRQ, geometry, controller, DMA/HDMA, PPU-port and audio assertions. Preserve cleared-game sources, pins, hashes, replay inputs, gameplay/music assertions, deadlines and tolerances. Use only original diagnostics or the existing licensed source-built fixtures; acquire no commercial ROM or firmware.

Remaining scheduler work includes late/line-spanning delivery and VTIME ownership, live timer writes, startup/reset alignment, TIMEUP disputes, NMI delays, refresh/startup revisions, physical access/recognition phases and full device synchronization, including APU advancement before raster processing.

Inventory scopes remain intact: `cpu`, `bus`, `scheduler`, `dma`, `hdma`, `controllers`, `ppu-bg`, `ppu-offset`, `ppu-hires`, `ppu-mode7`, `ppu-objects`, `ppu-color`, `ppu-ports`, `ppu-display`, `spc`, `ipl`, `dsp-voices`, `dsp-noise`, `dsp-pitch`, `dsp-envelope`, `dsp-echo` and `dsp-timing` remain partial; `ppu-raster` and `pal` remain unimplemented. No category becomes verified. Passing these bounded checks establishes neither full hardware accuracy nor commercial compatibility and does not complete Issue #3.

## Optional validation

The README's separate 301-second wall-clock browser test. No commercial-game acquisition or physical-device testing is required.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
